# Test bd claim: the exit-code contract in both direct and daemon mode.
# 0 = claimed/renewed, 3 = denied (deny_reason says retry vs skip), 1 = error.
bd init --prefix test

bd create 'Issue to claim'
cp stdout issue.txt
exec sh -c 'grep -oE "test-[a-z0-9]+" issue.txt > direct_id.txt'

# --- Direct mode (--no-daemon) ---

# Claiming an open issue wins.
exec sh -c 'bd --no-daemon claim $(cat direct_id.txt) --assignee alice; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'Claimed issue'
stdout 'exit=0'

# The holder claiming again renews instead of stealing from itself.
exec sh -c 'bd --no-daemon claim $(cat direct_id.txt) --assignee alice --lease 45m; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'Renewed issue'
stdout 'exit=0'

# A rival loses: exit 3, deny_reason=held, so a shell caller retries later.
exec sh -c 'bd --no-daemon claim $(cat direct_id.txt) --assignee bob 2>err.txt; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=3'
grep 'deny_reason=held' err.txt
grep 'held by alice' err.txt

# --json emits the outcome object on a denial too.
exec sh -c 'bd --no-daemon claim $(cat direct_id.txt) --assignee bob --json 2>/dev/null; echo exit=$?'
stdout '"outcome": "denied"'
stdout '"deny_reason": "held"'
stdout 'exit=3'

# A non-claimable status also exits 3, but deny_reason=status tells the caller to skip.
exec sh -c 'bd --no-daemon update $(cat direct_id.txt) --status blocked'
exec sh -c 'bd --no-daemon claim $(cat direct_id.txt) --assignee bob 2>err.txt; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=3'
grep 'deny_reason=status' err.txt
grep 'status blocked' err.txt

# An empty --assignee is a usage error, not a claim: two empty claimants would both win.
exec sh -c 'bd --no-daemon claim $(cat direct_id.txt) --assignee "" 2>err.txt; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=1'
grep 'assignee' err.txt

# A missing --assignee is the same usage error.
exec sh -c 'bd --no-daemon claim $(cat direct_id.txt) 2>err.txt; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=1'

# An unknown issue is an error, not a denial.
exec sh -c 'bd --no-daemon claim test-nosuch --assignee alice 2>err.txt; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=1'

# A closed issue is an error too: there is nothing to wait for.
exec sh -c 'bd --no-daemon close $(cat direct_id.txt) --reason done'
exec sh -c 'bd --no-daemon claim $(cat direct_id.txt) --assignee bob 2>err.txt; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=1'
grep 'closed' err.txt

# --- Daemon mode: same outcomes through the RPC op ---

bd daemon --start --local
bd daemon --status
stdout 'running'

bd create 'Issue to claim via daemon'
cp stdout daemon_issue.txt
exec sh -c 'grep -oE "test-[a-z0-9]+" daemon_issue.txt > daemon_id.txt'

exec sh -c 'bd claim $(cat daemon_id.txt) --assignee alice; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'Claimed issue'
stdout 'exit=0'

exec sh -c 'bd claim $(cat daemon_id.txt) --assignee alice; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'Renewed issue'
stdout 'exit=0'

exec sh -c 'bd claim $(cat daemon_id.txt) --assignee bob 2>err.txt; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=3'
grep 'deny_reason=held' err.txt

exec sh -c 'bd update $(cat daemon_id.txt) --status blocked'
exec sh -c 'bd claim $(cat daemon_id.txt) --assignee bob 2>err.txt; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=3'
grep 'deny_reason=status' err.txt

exec sh -c 'bd claim $(cat daemon_id.txt) --assignee "" 2>err.txt; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=1'

exec sh -c 'bd close $(cat daemon_id.txt) --reason done'
exec sh -c 'bd claim $(cat daemon_id.txt) --assignee bob 2>err.txt; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=1'
grep 'closed' err.txt

bd daemon --stop
